name: SNAPback
description: AI-powered cashback for 42 million SNAP/WIC families — rewarding sustained healthy grocery habits, not one-off purchases.
badges: George Hacks x United Nations "Reboot the Earth" Hackathon — Track 1 Grand Prize Winner

detailedSections.title: The problem.
detailedSections.content: 42 million Americans rely on SNAP/WIC every month. The cheapest, easiest item on the shelf is almost always the worst for them. Generic "eat more vegetables" guidance doesn't help a Caribbean grandmother shopping for callaloo or a South Asian household buying atta and dal on a $480 monthly budget. We built SNAPback in response to the United Nations FAO's problem statement on equitable, personalized nutrition.

detailedSections.title: The product.
detailedSections.content: SNAPback is a Flutter mobile app that turns every grocery receipt into personalized, culturally-aware nutrition guidance — and pays families real cashback when they sustain healthier shopping habits.

detailedSections.title: How it works.
content: Users sign up with their monthly SNAP budget, family size, and the cuisines they actually cook (24 supported — Caribbean, South Asian, West African, Latin American, East Asian, Middle Eastern, and more).

After every grocery trip, they scan a receipt. Google Gemini 2.5 Flash reads it multimodally — every item, quantity, and price — and scores each edible item 0–5 against a USDA-derived healthy-foods rubric in a single structured-JSON call.
Cashback is tiered: 5% for 5★ items, 3% for 4★, 1% for 3★, plus a +1 percentage-point cultural-match bonus.
Monthly cap: min(10% × SNAP amount, $25 × family size) — grounded in realistic public-benefits math.

detailedSections.title: The original idea: the Redemption Gate.
detailedSections.content: Most cashback apps pay for any purchase. SNAPback only unlocks the cashback if the user's monthly average health score stays at 4/5 or higher. We don't reward one good trip to the store — we reward sustained behavioral change. This is the policy lever that turns nutrition science into action.

detailedSections.title: Architecture.
content: Mobile (Flutter/Dart): MVVM with Provider; go_router + IndexedStack for persistent bottom-tab navigation; fl_chart for the monthly score ring; custom animated SnapbackLoader; full light/dark theming; accessibility labels on every key surface (screen readers announce the score ring, redemption badge, and trip rows).

Backend (Firebase Cloud Functions, Node 20, 2nd gen): Two functions. processReceipt triggers on Storage upload, calls Gemini 2.5 Flash with a strict JSON schema and a USDA-grounded system prompt (plus an explicit non-edible blocklist), and writes structured items to Firestore. scoreTrip triggers on that write, applies tiered cashback, computes the item-weighted monthly health average, evaluates the redemption gate, and generates culturally-matched recipe suggestions via a second Gemini call.

Data: Firebase Auth, Cloud Firestore with live streams powering real-time Dashboard/History/Trip Result (no pull-to-refresh anywhere), Firebase Storage for receipt images, Gemini API key in Firebase Secrets.

detailedSections.title: Open-source contribution.
detailedSections.content: Several Flutter widgets we relied on were broken or abandoned on pub.dev. Instead of working around them, we rewrote and open-sourced the fixes — which is why we specifically took home the Open Source track prize.

detailedSections.title: Hard problems we solved.
content: Replaced a failed traditional OCR + separate scoring pipeline with a single multimodal Gemini call that outputs structured JSON grounded in USDA criteria.
Fixed a Firestore race condition by writing the trip document before uploading the image to Storage.
Rewrote an over-generous cashback model into a per-item tiered system with a SNAP-proportional monthly cap and the redemption gate — sustainable enough to actually ship as a public-benefits program.
Added server-side non-edible blocklists so toilet paper and detergent don't inflate health scores.
